title: Disaster restore proof
description: Objective: prove complete backup generations, two-slot recovery anchors, fresh incarnation/key epochs, orphan inventory, and quiesced recovery after media loss. Deliverable: CORE-S14 restore fixtures and evidence. NOT in scope: ordinary restart or optimistic orphan adoption. Hard dependencies: full store/artifact/effect inventory implementations. Owned paths: tests/fault/disaster-restore/** and backup tooling paths. Verification: pnpm test:fault.
definitionOfDone: Crash at every prepare/install/fsync/switch boundary exposes either old authority or one verified quiesced restore, never a mixture.
Repeated same-generation restore uses fresh incarnation/key epochs and all stale grants fail.
Missing inventory or artifact/key proof keeps recovery unavailable with UNKNOWN_TRUTH.
taskRails: Claims follow the benchmark permit-list; missing, partial, cross-basis, or unverifiable evidence is UNKNOWN, never PASS.
No confirmatory corpus is generated or viewed until the implementation commit is frozen exactly as specified.
GO_QUIESCE and GO_ACTIVATE are separate human decisions. Keep evidence exact, reproducible, and scoped to one source commit.
reopenReason:
Restoring architect-8a4a1764's original block. The 11:40Z BLOCKED->PLANNING transition was an unintended side effect of moe.unblock_worker, which flips the TASK out of BLOCKED when a WORKER is unblocked. The human was freeing a stuck worker and did not intend to re-queue this task; confirmed at 11:58Z. Mechanism found by architect-8c9073cd.

THE BLOCK STANDS ON ITS ORIGINAL EVIDENCE, which I re-verified independently on disk at 11:29Z rather than reading off the block note. What EXISTS is vocabulary: recovery.restore_quiesce and recovery.complete as a contract union (packages/core/src/project/project-contract.ts:11-12); RestoreQuiesceWitness and RecoveryCompletionWitness shapes; two reducer transitions (project-reducer.ts:35-36); shape guards in project-validation.ts; and a command builder in the generated control-room client. What does NOT exist is the controller: nothing mints an incarnation, installs a slot, or advances a key epoch. grep for mintIncarnation/slotInstall/keyEpoch returns only the recoveryIncarnationRef FIELD inside the witness shapes.

A proof planned against this today would certify the shapes, which Clause 2 explicitly forbids: "a proof that only proves the shapes is worse than no proof — it retires the gap." architect-8a4a1764's read was exact and does not need redoing.

Required output is a prerequisite production task for the restore controller, with the gap measured symbol by symbol. That authoring is in flight — architect-8c9073cd is routing platform and doctor-inventory prerequisites in the same family, and this one belongs beside them.

architect-f39f0c46 held this task in PLANNING when the flip was reversed; they lose no work, since the hold I posted at 11:57Z asked them to wait before spending a context load on it. Unblock when the restore controller exists and is verifiable by grep or probe, not on a status flip.

comments.author: governor-fce4d563
comments.content:
GOVERNANCE — read before planning. This task returned to PLANNING after architect-8a4a1764 blocked it. The block was correct and governance upheld it (#governors msg-52d7aef8). Do NOT re-derive the audit; it costs a full context load to reach the same answer.

THE FINDING, measured on disk 2026-08-09, not read off the design:
  EXISTS — project-contract.ts declares commands recovery.restore_quiesce and recovery.complete, plus RestoreQuiesceWitness {backupGenerationHash, recoveryIncarnationRef, truthClass} and RecoveryCompletionWitness {coverageProofHash, inventoryReconciliationHash, recoveryDecisionRef, ...}. project-reducer.ts:35,162 admits the transition and calls quiesce(). project-validation.ts:166,171 are exact-key SHAPE guards. Real fsync exists, but only in the artifact CAS.
  DOES NOT EXIST — grep over packages/*/src and apps/*/src, zero hits each: recoveryAnchor / "recovery anchor" (the objective needs TWO-SLOT anchors and DoD 1 needs a crash at every prepare/install/fsync/switch boundary — no slot-install protocol exists); keyEpoch / "key epoch" (DoD 2 needs fresh key epochs with stale grants failing — recoveryIncarnationRef is a string field in a witness, nothing MINTS an incarnation).

The witness shapes are the vocabulary of a restore. The controller that performs one is absent. quiesce() recording that a restore happened is not a restore.

WHAT NOT TO DO, both explicitly rejected by QA in advance (qa-812c17a0, #general msg-a4b06362): (a) reimplementing the controller inside a test fixture — a direct epic rail 6 violation, rejected on sight; (b) narrowing the DoD to "shape guards accept well-formed witnesses" — worse than (a), because it ships a green label over an untested mechanism. There is nothing to inject faults into, so there is no evidence to be had, and unverifiable evidence is UNKNOWN, never PASS. QA has stated they will not approve a task whose DoD requires proving a behaviour no production surface performs.

REQUIRED OUTPUT INSTEAD: file the prerequisite production tasks, then leave this one blocked with their ids and an unblock trigger. At minimum a two-slot recovery anchor with its prepare/install/fsync/switch protocol, and key-epoch minting with stale-grant refusal; architect-8a4a1764's handoff (mem:task-task-0c89476b78044024b07c86c0c8986bd0-handoff) names the rest. Bound each as composition over existing core symbols where possible, and measure each gap symbol by symbol before writing the ticket.

PRECEDENT TO COPY: architect-0b81de40 did exactly this off the Foundation canary's block report — three CRITICAL tickets (task-671578e5, task-9011e3b3, task-39fe2da5), each with the gap measured on disk and scoped as composition rather than new domain logic. Two are being coded now. That is the play; see task-97554aa4 comment-b6b518a5 for the shape of the block record.

This is the fourth instance of one pattern — vocabulary present, capability absent — and it is the subject of pending rail proposal prop-d68b105c.
